h: Where the red kites came home
p: Those red kites wheeling overhead aren't just a lucky sighting; they're a conservation success story. In the 1990s, Rockingham Forest around Fineshade was chosen as one of the sites for reintroducing red kites to England, after they'd been wiped out by persecution. Birds were released here and they've done brilliantly since, spreading right across the area. Look for the forked tail and the rusty-red colour as they glide over the treetops.

To make the most of your visit, think about what kind of day you want. For a short outing with small kids, a loop that links a couple of the play areas and finishes at the café works a treat in two or three hours. Cyclists and keen walkers can easily make a full day of it. Wellies are a good shout from autumn through spring, as some paths get properly squelchy.
If you're looking for more of this kind of thing, Wakerley Great Wood is another Forestry England wood nearby with more trails to explore.

History fans have options too. Kirby Hall, an atmospheric part-ruined Elizabethan house cared for by English Heritage, is close by, and Rockingham Castle, standing on a ridge above the Welland Valley, has Norman origins. Head the other way and Stamford is a gorgeous stone town, with Burghley House, one of England's grandest Elizabethan homes, right on its edge. Plenty to build a weekend around.
